summary: Announces that the network address of MIT-Multics would change from 6 to 44 on a Monday in December 1973, as a second MIT IMP came into use. Sites were asked to update their tables and programs.

eli5.summary: A computer moved to a new house number on the network, so this note told everyone to update their address books.

subtitle: MIT-Multics moves to a new network address to balance load

tldr.problem: The IMP serving MIT (Interface Message Processor number 6) was overloaded, with nine uses for its four available ports and four very active hosts trying to use it.
tldr.mechanism: MIT-Multics, one of the active hosts on IMP 6, was moved to a new IMP (number 44) on December 17, 1973. This required all network users and sites to update their host tables and programs with the new network address.
tldr.outcome: The load was distributed more evenly across the IMPs. MIT-Multics became reachable at address 44 instead of address 6.

today: RFC 590 is a brief but important document showing the logistical challenges of the early ARPANET, where network changes like address reassignments required advance notice and careful coordination. MIT-Multics was a historically significant system in early computing, and this RFC marks a moment in its operational history on ARPANET.

sections.title: Address Change Announcement
sections.content:
MIT-Multics, an important host on the ARPANET, is changing its network address from 6 to 44 (decimal) on Monday, December 17, 1973. All sites that have the MIT-Multics address in their host tables, network code, or programs must update these entries before the changeover date.

The author, M. Padlipsky, asks for the network's patience during the transition and apologizes for the inconvenience.
sections.eli5: An important computer at MIT is moving to a new address on the network, and everyone needs to update their lists.

sections.title: Reasons for the Move
sections.content: The change was made necessary by three factors. First, IMP 6 was overloaded: there were nine different network services needing its four available ports, making the addition of a second MIT IMP desirable. Second, IMP 6 had four very active hosts, and moving at least one of them to the new, less busy IMP would improve performance and availability. Third, the new Multics machine is located about 2000 feet from the old IMP, while the new Multics location is much closer to the new (less busy) IMP.
sections.eli5: The old network connection point at MIT was crowded and had too many computers on it, so the Multics computer moved to a new, less busy connection point.

sections.title: Transition Plan and Testing
sections.content:
It is likely that one or two additional test sessions will be run on the new IMP prior to the changeover date of December 17. These test sessions will be announced in the MIT-Multics "message of the day" and would temporarily affect only users who are unable to employ numeric host addresses directly (i.e., users who rely on looking up the address by name rather than knowing the numeric address to enter directly).

Users who use numeric addresses in their code and can easily change them should prepare to make those changes on the changeover date. Sites that rely on name services should check that their name service is updated.
sections.eli5: Before the big move, there will be some test runs so problems can be found early. On December 17, the address will officially change, and anyone who looks up the address by name will still be fine, but anyone with the address hardcoded in their programs will need to update.
